subject: ventures/driving-instructor-lesson-pricing-calculator
professional: an accountant or bookkeeper who keeps the books for self-employed driving instructors (UK ADIs and US behind-the-wheel instructors who own a dual-control car). First checks: are all vehicle costs captured per mile and per year (fuel, wear, insurance, depreciation or lease, franchise fee), is the per-mile figure plausible against a published benchmark such as the IRS standard mileage rate, is a 'take-home' target grossed up for self-employment tax, and does the tool work in the units the instructor actually buys fuel in.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python recomputation from first principles (scratchpad/indep.py) of the page's worked example ($50, 60 min + 15 min gap, 25 slots x 46 weeks, 8% unpaid cancellations, 12 mi, 40 mpg, $4/gal, $0.10/mi wear, $4,600 fixed, $30k target, block 10 for $450): paid lessons 1,058; running 2.40; fixed per paid lesson 4.35; cost 6.75; profit per lesson 43.25; annual profit 45,760.80; diary hours 1,437.5; profit per diary hour 31.83; break-even 6.75; target price 35.10; block profit per lesson 38.25; year at block rate 40,470.80. The engine (node scratchpad/tool.mjs) returns every figure identically. 90-minute $75 lesson -> $50 hourly equivalent, by hand. Per-mile cross-check against IRS 2025 standard mileage rate (70 cents, IRS Notice 2025-5): the example's all-in vehicle cost is (1,058 x 2.40 + 4,600) / 12,696 mi = $0.562/mi, below but plausible against 70 cents. The arithmetic is right for what it models, so 3; the gaps are in what the labels promise (take-home, ADI units) and the page's silent defaults, scored under claims, fitness and craft.
evidence.completeness: Features claimed in README/llms.txt/page checked by engine run and code read: paid lessons, revenue, running and fixed cost per paid lesson, profit per lesson and per diary hour, annual profit, break-even, target price, block-discount check with findings (all present and computed); copy summary with clipboard fallback (index.html:298-316); load example and clear (index.html:280-296); usage counting with opt-out (usage.mjs, usage.test.mjs pass). No TODOs or stubs. Every claimed feature works end to end.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/driving-instructor-lesson-pricing-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 32/32 pass, 93 ms. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: wear not scaled by miles caught; profit-per-diary-hour denominator drops the unpaid gap SURVIVED; block 'year if every lesson at block rate' uses slots instead of paid lessons SURVIVED; loss finding threshold 0 -> -1000 SURVIVED; cancellation finding's full-diary comparison uses paid lessons SURVIVED; 52-week cap -> 53 SURVIVED. 5 of 6 survived, including profit per diary hour (a headline output on the page) and the block-year figure. The money path (paid lessons, running, fixed, annual profit, break-even, target) is well pinned; page.test.mjs only string-matches the HTML, so readInputs and its silent defaults are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (150 lines), index.html script (185-331), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Engine is small, pure, validates non-negative and non-zero inputs with readable errors. Defects: the page's readInputs (index.html:222-236) defeats that validation with `Number(...) || default`: a blank or 0 weeks becomes 46, blank or 0 lesson minutes becomes 60, blank fuel price and blank miles become 0 without a message, although the status line asks for both (the Calculate guard at index.html:273 checks only price, slots and mpg). The engine itself also accepts '' as 0 (Number('') === 0; priceLessons({...fuelPrice:''}) -> running cost 1.20, fuel dropped). money() is duplicated in index.html:191 and calc.mjs:27.
evidence.claims: Checked: disclaimer in footer (index.html:175) and in the copied summary (calc.mjs:148), pass; 'nothing uploaded', no network calls in the script, pass; usage events named in README match record() calls, pass; served llms.txt and canonicals (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) have no placeholder or retired origin, pass (the duncan-haywood.github.io link in source llms.txt is source-only). Fail: 'the price that reaches your take-home target' (index.html:7, index.html:12 JSON-LD, llms.txt:3, README.md:5) while the target is profit before income tax and self-employment tax (index.html:117, 155); for a US instructor a $30,000 pre-tax profit carries $4,238.87 SE tax (Schedule SE: 30,000 x 0.9235 x 0.153), so the 'take-home' price is $39.77, not $35.10. Partial: README.md:3 and calc.mjs:5 name ADIs (the UK term) as the buyer, but the page takes only $ and US gallons with no litre or imperial-gallon option. Wear default $0.10/mile is uncited.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as a US behind-the-wheel instructor: enter price, slots, miles, mpg, fuel, fixed costs -> a clear profit per lesson, break-even and target price in one click, copyable. Usable for a first price. Gaps in the first hour: a UK ADI buys fuel in GBP per litre and quotes imperial mpg; typing GBP 1.45/litre and 50 mpg into the '$ per gallon' box gives fuel 2.9p/mile instead of 13.2p (understated 4.55x, the litres per imperial gallon); the 'take-home' target ignores SE tax; cancelled lessons carry no running cost although late cancellations and no-shows are usually driven to; no tax set-aside, VAT-threshold or admin-time view.
evidence.domain: Method compared with standard cost-plus / break-even pricing for a sole trader and with the IRS split of vehicle costs into per-mile (fuel, wear) and fixed (insurance, depreciation, registration): the model spreads fixed costs over paid lessons, charges running costs per paid lesson, and solves price = (target + fixed)/paid + running, which is the textbook form and recomputes exactly. Departs: profit target is pre-tax while labelled take-home; running cost assumed zero on cancelled slots; no unit support for UK users the README names. Within the stated before-tax limit an accountant would accept the method.

defects.what: The target price is sold as reaching a 'take-home' target (meta description, JSON-LD, llms.txt, README; the input label itself does say before tax, index.html:117) but the target is profit before income tax and self-employment tax; a US instructor wanting $30,000 after SE tax needs $39.77 a lesson, not the $35.10 shown.

Page silently substitutes defaults for blank or zero inputs (Number(...) || 46/60/0): blank fuel price or miles drops fuel cost to 0, a typed 0 weeks becomes 46, bypassing the engine's validation; the Calculate guard checks only price, slots and mpg.
README and calc.mjs name UK ADIs as buyers, but inputs are $ and US gallons only; a UK instructor entering per-litre fuel price understates fuel cost 4.55x with no warning.

Profit per diary hour (a headline output) is untested: dropping the unpaid gap from the denominator leaves all 32 tests green; so do the block-year figure, the loss-finding threshold and the cancellation finding's full-diary comparison.
Running cost is charged only on paid lessons; late cancellations and no-shows that are driven to carry fuel and wear the model leaves out.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: an independent recomputation of the worked example reproduces every output to the cent (paid lessons 1,058, cost 6.75 per lesson, annual profit 45,760.80, target price 35.10, profit per diary hour 31.83), and the all-in $0.56/mile sits plausibly under the IRS 70-cent rate. It falls short of an instructor's accountant on what the labels promise: the target is called 'take-home' in the meta description, llms.txt and README while it is pre-tax ($39.77 vs $35.10 for a US $30k after SE tax), UK ADIs are named as buyers but only $ and US gallons are accepted, and the page silently replaces blank or zero inputs with defaults. Five of six seeded mutants survived, including profit per diary hour. Finished (completeness 3), below the bar (claims 2, verification 2).
